fade_years.why: Margin and growth normalisation after a commodity-driven year plausibly takes most of a decade as new fields replace decline, so 8 years.

long_run_op_margin.why: Long-run margin is set near the 11-year median of about 0.23, trimmed for rising depreciation and for the mix shift toward lower-margin power and trading. The 2022 peak of 0.5226 is treated as non-recurring.

op_margin.why: Q3 2026 net operating income was very strong, so 2026 margin is set well above the 2025 level of 0.2381. It then fades toward a mid-cycle level as prices normalise and depreciation and impairments stay elevated, in line with the base rate that a margin above the long-run median keeps only part of the gap.

quotes.quote: Return on new investment at which growth adds no value (code, after the company's leverage): 0.0550

return_on_new_investment_long_run.why: The base-year return on tangible capital of 0.1253 benefited from an asset base partly depreciated and from price strength. New investment in power, international and deepwater projects should earn less, but still above the 0.0550 break-even.

rev_growth.why: Production growth guidance was raised to about 4% and Q3 prices were higher, so year 1 (2026) growth is strong. Later years assume price normalisation, with modest volume growth only partly offsetting it. Q3 volume growth was 2%, below the full-year guide, which tempers the volume assumption.

terminal_growth.why: A mature integrated oil and gas producer with a declining NCS base should grow below the 0.0375 nominal anchor, so about 2% is used.

risks.risk: Oil and gas prices fall back toward the lower end of the cycle, compressing margins well below the 2021-2025 median
Unplanned outages, faster NCS decline, or further impairments on updated production profiles cut volumes and revenue
Margins in the near years revert faster to the 2025 level than assumed, with 2026 price strength proving temporary

debt_level_representative.why: Debt of about USD 30 billion against USD 40 billion equity and about USD 20 billion of operating cash flow is moderate, though 2025 saw new borrowing of 5,915 after none in the two prior years.

situation.margin_position: The 2025 operating margin of 0.2381 is below the 5-year median of 0.3338, which is lifted by the 2021-2022 price spike, and close to the 11-year median of about 0.23. It has fallen each year since 2022 as prices normalised and depreciation and purchases rose. Q3 2026 net operating income of USD 11.95 billion suggests 2026 margins are well above 2025 on higher prices.

tax_rate_representative.why: Income tax took most of pre-tax income (20,030 of 25,088) because of high Norwegian petroleum taxation, which is likely to persist on the shelf, but the mix shift toward international and power assets could lower it.

situation.why: 2025 was a mid-to-low point in the commodity cycle (net operating income 25,352 against 35,770 in 2023), and the 2026 interim results show a strong rebound on higher prices and production. Below-median margins in cyclical names tend to revert quickly, so year 1 is set above the base year and then fades back toward a mid-cycle level. A 2026 price boost is not assumed to persist.
